pr_body:
Bug fixes and improvements for the hawkbit subsys.

Fixes:

- #37327
- #37272
- #37225
   - 1 - The hawkbit_init function is assuming the "storage" label to be with DT_CHOSEN_ZEPHYR_FLASH_CONTROLLER_LABEL (usually flash0?) whereas it can can be with the external serial flash so this should follows where the "storage" is defined instead of a constant.
   - 2 - Similar to 1
   - 3 - Removes a typo (extra space)
   - 7 - LOG_MODULE_REGISTER(hawkbit); is wrong, its verbosity can't be configured
 - (sample) Add missing header
 - (sample) Remove unused variable

Improvements
- Verify SHA256 hash of the downloaded image to determine if the download is successful before asking the bootloader to perform an upgrade.

Closes #37272
Closes #37327

issue_context.title: subsys/mgmt/hawkbit: Falsely determine that an update is installed successfully
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
`hawkbit` determines that an update is installed and ready for reboot even though it only downloaded and written 5.75% of the image into the flash.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
I testing the `hawkbit` sample with a STM32G0B1RE custom board with a GSM (LTE) modem (Quectel EC21). `image-1` slot is in an external `spi-nor` flash.

**Expected behavior**
Downloads the OTA target firmware successfully, and can be applied to primary slot after `kernel reboot cold`

**Impact**
Unable to use `hawkbit`

**Logs and console output**
[hawkbit_log.txt](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/6891871/hawkbit_log.txt)


**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows 10
 - Toolchain: gnuarmemb
 - v2.6.0-rc2-107-gebe282b02d9f


**Additional context**
Ubuntu 20.04, running `hawkbit` in a docker following the `hawkbit`'s sample `README`
`hawkbit` external port is changed to `9010` instead of the default `8080`, sitting behind nginx reverse proxy such that it can be access from hawkbit.mydomain.com with SSL. (shouldn't matter since the device access `hawkbit` using raw IP)
comments:
I don't have a full picture of how this works yet.

I know that it should stay in the `response_cb` and will not reach the [line](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/mgmt/hawkbit/hawkbit.c#L1211) where it determines whether the download passed or failed. Apparently this check has failed its purpose, so maybe we need something more robust? e.g. Check if the downloaded & written image size matches its actual size?

Another thing that I noticed is that the `hawkbit` server thinks that the device retrieved the image even though it is still downloading. Problem arises when the download fails: the device will not be able to redownload the image again, I'm not sure if this is the problem of the `hawkbit` server or the Zephyr's implementation.

If this is something related to the client implementation instead, this should be made into another issue.

I notice that `&hb_context.semaphore` isn't used anywhere within the `hawkbit` subsys.

@Navin-Sankar Is that meant to signal the completion of the download in `hawkbit_probe` ?
